<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par69 />vowel ''ŭ'' coalesces into ''û''; so throughout {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הוּשַׁב}} for ''hŭwšabh''; but with a preceding ''a'' the {{GHGterm|Wāw}} is contracted into ''ô'' ({{GHGheb|text=וֹ}}); so in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle Niphʿal}} and throughout {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נוֹשַׁב}} from an original ''năwšăbh'', {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשִׁיב}} from an original ''hăwšîbh''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|k}}
The first radical always appears as {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle Qal}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָשַׁב}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=יֹשֵׁב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָשׁוּב}}, even when {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} precedes, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וְיָשַׁב}} (but {{GHGheb|text=וִיֽשַׁבְתֶּם}}, according to {{GHGpar|24|b}}), also throughout {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִחֵל|translate=to wait}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֻלַּד|translate=to be born}}, and in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=יְיַחֵל}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְיֻדָּע|translate=known}} (from {{GHGheb|text=יָדַע}}), and, as a rule, also in ''Hithpaʿel'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְיַלֵּד}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְיַצֵּב}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְיַחֵשׂ}} (as against {{GHGheb|text=הִתְוַדַּע}}, &c., with {{GHGterm|Wāw}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|l}}
The beginner may recognize verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} partly by the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} under the preformatives; in {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} by the {{GHGterm|Wāw}} ({{GHGheb|text=ו}}, {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}}) before the second radical. (The defective writing, as in {{GHGheb|text=הֹלִיד}}, is rare.) Verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} have forms like {{GHGheb|text=(דַּע) שֵׁב}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫בֶת}}, in common with verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}. Similarly {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} has the same form as in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|m}}
Rem. 1. The {{GHGterm|infinitive Qal}} of the weaker form ({{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫בֶת}}, ground-form ''šibt'', {{GHGheb|text=רֶ֫שֶׁת}}; cf. above, c) with suffixes is pointed as {{GHGheb|text=שִׁבְתִּי}},<ref>{{GHGheb|text=וְשַׁבְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=23|verse=6}} can hardly be intended for an ''infin.'' with suffix from {{GHGheb|text=יָשַׁב}}, but rather for a ''perf. consec.'' from {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּב}}; but read {{GHGheb|text=וְיָֽשַׁבְתִּי}}.</ref> {{GHGheb|text=רִשְׁתּוֹ}} (the strong form only in {{GHGheb|text=לְיָרְשֵׁ֫נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=15}}). The masculine form is very rare, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דֵּעַ|translate=to know}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=32|verse=6.10}}, as also the feminine ending {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דֵּעָ֫ה}}<ref>The infinitives {{GHGheb|text=דֵּעָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=רְדָה}} belong to the source marked E (Dillmann’s B) in the modern criticism of the Pentateuch. The same document also has {{GHGheb|text=נְתֹן|translate=to give}}, for {{GHGheb|text=תֵּת}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֲלֹךְ|translate=to go}}, for {{GHGheb|text=לֶ֫כֶת}}; and {{GHGheb|text=עֲשׂה|translate=to make}}, for {{GHGheb|text=עֲשׂוֹת}}. See Dillmann, {{GHGcite|title=Die BB. Num., Deut., Jos.}}, p. 618.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=4}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֵדָ֫ה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=3}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=19|verse=3}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=9|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽרְדָה}}<sup>2</sup> ''to descend'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=3}}, where the change of the ''ē'' into vocal {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} is to be explained, with König, from its position between the principal and secondary tone. From {{GHGheb|text=יָדַע}}, under the influence of the guttural, {{GHGheb|text=דַּ֫עַת}} is formed, with ''suff.'' {{GHGheb|text=דַּעְתִּי}}, &c.; but from {{GHGheb|text=יצא}}, {{GHGheb|text=צֵאת}}. From {{GHGheb|text=יָרַד}} there occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=30|verse=4}} in {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=מִיָּרְדִי}} (the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} requires {{GHGheb|text=מִיּֽוֹרְדֵי}}) a very remarkable case of the strong form (for {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽרִדְתִּי}}). For {{GHGheb|text=לַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=19}} (generally explained as a case of assimilation of {{GHGheb|text=ד}} to {{GHGheb|text=ת}} in the supposed ground-form ''ladt''; according to Mayer Lambert pausal of {{GHGheb|text=לֵת}}=''lidt'', see above, c) read simply {{GHGheb|text=לֶ֫דֶת}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|n}}
Examples of the strong form of the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} are {{GHGheb|text=יְרֹא|translate=to fear}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=22|verse=25}}, with preposition {{GHGheb|text=לִיסֹד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=16}} (but {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=31|verse=7}} according to Ben Naphtali {{GHGheb|text=לִיסֹּד}}, where the {{GHGheb|text=י}} is only retained orthographically, but is really assimilated to the {{GHGheb|text=ס}}; the reading of Ben Asher, {{GHGheb|text=לְיִסּוֹד}}, accepted by Baer, is meaningless); {{GHGheb|text=לִישׁוֹן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=5|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֵרֹא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=29}} is irregular, but probably {{GHGheb|text=לִרֹא}} (for {{GHGheb|text=לִירֹא}}) is intended. With ''suff.'' {{GHGheb|text=בְּיָסְדִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=4}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=3|verse=12}}; with {{GHGheb|text=ת}} {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=יְכֹ֫לֶת|translate=to be able}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=16}}. On {{GHGheb|text=יְבֹ֫שֶׁת}}, which is likewise usually referred to this class, cf. the note on {{GHGpar|70|a}}.
